steps.text: Print displays the words inside the quotation marks: Hello, research! Change those words to make your own greeting, keeping both quotation marks and both parentheses.
This assigns the number three to goals. The equals sign stores a value under a name so a later line can use it.
This stores five in attempts. The attempt count includes every shot, whether it scored or missed.
Divide goals by attempts, then multiply by one hundred to calculate a percentage. Three out of five gives sixty, which Python stores in rate.
Print looks up rate and displays sixty point zero. The decimal point comes from division; this is the percentage calculated on the previous line.
This list stores five synthetic attempts in order. One means a goal and zero means a miss; there are three goals and two misses.
Sum adds the list entries, and print displays three. Adding zeros and ones counts goals because each goal contributes one.
Len counts the entries, and print displays five. A miss still counts as an attempt, even though its value is zero.
This divides the goal count by the attempt count and multiplies by one hundred. Print displays sixty point zero, describing the percentage for this synthetic sample.
These lists store the synthetic shots for near, middle, and far distances. Each has five attempts. Counting the ones gives four, three, and two goals respectively.
Sum counts the goals in each distance group. This new list stores those three totals in order: four, three, and two.
Print displays the label Goals and the list of totals. Match each position with its distance group: near first, middle second, and far third.
The three goal totals add to nine. Dividing by three groups gives a mean of three goals per five-shot group. This output is neither meters nor a percentage.
Max finds the largest goal total, four, and min finds the smallest, two. Print labels both results so we can tell which summary each number represents.
This imports the plotting tools from Matplotlib and gives them the short name p l t. The later drawing commands use that name.
These lines define the same three groups of synthetic shots inside this program. Including them here lets this chart run independently of the earlier slides.
This compact expression visits each shot list, divides its goal count by its attempt count, and multiplies by one hundred. Rates becomes eighty, sixty, and forty.
Bar draws one bar for each distance label using the corresponding rate as its height. The color list gives each bar its own color; it does not change the data.
This labels the vertical axis Success rate, with a percent sign. The label tells a reader how to interpret the bar heights.
This sets the vertical axis from zero to one hundred. Showing the complete percentage scale helps readers judge the differences between the bars.
Show displays the completed chart. Check that the labels, bar heights, and scale agree with the records and calculations above.
